questions: Did s-bend and slalom runs still end off track with line_loss_events at 0, and at what step and bend does max_error first reach about 0.06 m?
Did oval steering_oscillation fall from 0.327 to 0.3 or below, and did oval progress hold near 0.71?
Did the larger footprint change completion_time or finish rate on oval, and did any s-bend or slalom run go past progress 0.2?
Does the controller look too slow to correct at the drift point, or does the centroid look too coarse on gentle bends?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If off-track on s-bend and slalom persists with losses at 0 and oscillation at or below 0.3, the next geometry test is to widen the inner sensors to ±0.04 m at this footprint, since the remaining failure is at the edge, not in the loss logic. If oval oscillation rises above 0.33 or oval progress falls below 0.5, revert sensor_size to 0.012 m.

intent: Keep the iteration 5 geometry, which removed line losses on the tight tracks, and change only the sensor footprint from 12 mm to 16 mm. The aim is to stop the robot drifting to the 0.06 m off-track edge on s-bend and slalom while still on the line, and to bring oval oscillation back to 0.3 or below without losing oval progress.
learning: Iteration 5 shows that the ±0.06 m span removes line losses on s-bend and slalom (0.0 per run, down from 0.9 to 1.0), so the span is correct. The problem has moved from losing the tape to drifting off the 0.06 m edge while still reading it. Body width cannot raise that floor, because the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m across the allowed body range. The next levers are footprint size and, if needed, the inner sensor spacing.
rationale: Iteration 5 (±0.06 m outer sensors, ±0.03 m inner, 12 mm footprints, y 0.04 m, 12 cm track) scored 151.91, the best so far. The evidence changed from the pre-race feedback. Line losses on s-bend and slalom fell from 0.9 to 1.0 per run to 0.0, and oval losses stayed at 0.0. The span change therefore did what it was meant to do. The remaining failure is different: every s-bend and slalom trial still ends off track (progress 0.18 and 0.12). Max_error sits at about 0.061 m, which is the off-track floor, while the tape is still being read. So the robot is drifting to the edge while still on the line, rather than losing the tape. Body width cannot move this floor: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) is still 0.06 m even at the 0.18 m maximum body width. Oval steering oscillation is 0.327, just above the 0.3 limit, while s-bend and slalom oscillation is about 0.15, so the controller has room on the tight tracks. I keep the ±0.06 m span, which removed the losses, and change one variable: sensor_size from 0.012 m to 0.016 m. Larger footprints overlap more, so each sensor's reading changes more smoothly as the edge of the tape crosses it. That should give the controller an earlier and smoother centroid on bends, which may reduce the drift to the edge and the oval jitter. Position, count, wheel_track (0.12 m) and y (0.04 m) stay fixed, since earlier tests showed narrowing the track or moving forward cut oval progress. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.06 m, or at least runs that progress further before going off track, with oval oscillation at or below 0.3 and oval progress holding near 0.7. Risk: a larger footprint may blur the centroid on gentle bends and reduce oval progress.
